page.content:
Gironde region of cabernet–merlot blends and the 1855 classification.

How Bordeaux connects

  • Topic: Old World wine — Bordeaux is a core Old World region of blended reds and sweet whites.
  • Item: Cabernet Sauvignon — Cabernet Sauvignon leads the great Left Bank Bordeaux blends.
  • Item: 1855 Classification — The 1855 Classification ranked Médoc and Sauternes châteaux of Bordeaux.
  • Character: Robert Parker — Parker's Wine Advocate scores moved the Bordeaux market in particular.
  • Event: Judgment of Paris — Paris 1976 put California cabernet above classed-growth Bordeaux in a blind vote.

What is Bordeaux?

Bordeaux is the Left and Right Bank of the Gironde: cabernet-led Médoc, merlot-led Saint-Émilion and Pomerol, and a château culture the New World still copies.

Key threads lead to Old World wine, Cabernet Sauvignon, 1855 Classification, Robert Parker and Judgment of Paris.
